title: The map of the landmines
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Who tells you where the landmines are before you speak?

I said that the person in the book has to make an apology, and that his public relations manager tells him: you have to kill this nonsense, we have to make a statement. Such managers play a critical role in the perception of public figures.
Good ones write scripts for their candidates, I said. They tell them what to wear and what not to wear, what to say. They are very involved in the public persona of whoever the celebrity is.
A student said: it is like the original chatbot, preempting you on everything you would need to know.
As one individual, I said, you can't see the big picture of everything around you. I told of going to a meeting where I pulled a public relations manager I knew aside and asked: who's here?

She ran down a map: the environmental organizations, the government, the executives, three senators you have to be careful with. They literally map out the landmines, the people on your side and not, and the ones who could be detrimental to you in a speech.

If you're with the media, I said, you need to know whether they are going to angle. Media is all over the place, from the far left to the far right. We need to know the intent of journalists, because there is always a political side, whatever your business.

A student said they didn't think there was an initial intent; he was looking for something to spin into a bigger story. I gave my own take, that the consequence was alarming, and that I thought the intent was malign. I added it was only my take.
Who maps the landmines for you?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write who is in the room when you speak publicly.
Write who is with you, against you, or uncertain.
Write the person who could map it for you.
Write what you want a journalist to understand.
Write what you would not say if it appeared tomorrow.

check.q: What did I say good public relations managers do?
choices: Write scripts and tell you what to say and wear

check.q: What did the manager in my story map?
choices: The people in the room who are on your side and not

check.q: What did I say you need to know about journalists?

recap: Map the landmines before you speak. Know the intent of the person who interviews you.
